title: Eph 2: good works are fruit of new creation—so sanctification too is by faith not works
source_text: XL. Praeterea postquam Apostolus, verbis ex epistola ad Ephesios allegatis, posuit nos salvatos esse fide, & non ex operibus, hoc inde confirmat, quod bona nostra opera sunt salutis nostrae fructus atque effectus, adeoque causa ejus esse non possunt. Ipsius enim inquit factura sumus: creati in Christo Jesu ad bona opera, quae praeparavit Deus ut in illis ambulemus. Quibus verbis significat opus esse ut per Dei gratiam praeparemur, atque instauramur, quae est novae cujusdam creationis species, priusquam possimus bona opera exercere. Nam in ultimis Apostoli verbis hypallage quaedam est, ac dum ait, Deum bona opera praeparasse, ut in illis ambulemus, dicere vult Deum nos gratia sua praeparare, ut ambulemus in bonis operibus. Haec vero ratio non minus clare probat nos sanctificari fide, & non ex operibus. Nam eodem plane modo, bona nostra opera non sunt causa, sed fructus nostrae sanctificationis, per quam ex impiis, quales natura sumus, vere sancti & justi reddimur. Atque, ut dixit Augustinus, bona opera sequi justificatum, non praecedere justificandum, ita quoque dicere possumus eadem bona opera sanctificandum non praecedere, sed sequi sanctificatum. Quia non prius bene operamur, quam Deus nos sua gratia sanctificet: sed Deus nos sua gratia sanctificat, ut postea bene operari possimus.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, after the Apostle, in the words alleged from the epistle to the Ephesians, has set down that we have been saved by faith and not of works, he confirms this from the fact that our good works are the fruit and effect of our salvation, and therefore cannot be its cause. For we are, he says, his workmanship: created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them. By which words he signifies that there is need that we be prepared and restored by God's grace—which is a kind of new creation—before we can exercise good works. For in the Apostle's last words there is a certain hypallage, and when he says that God prepared good works that we should walk in them, he means to say that God prepares us by his grace that we should walk in good works. But this reason no less clearly proves that we are sanctified by faith and not of works. For in exactly the same way our good works are not the cause but the fruit of our sanctification, through which from the impious, such as we are by nature, we are rendered truly holy and just. And as Augustine said that good works follow the justified, they do not precede the one to be justified, so also we can say that the same good works do not precede the one to be sanctified, but follow the sanctified. Because we do not first work well before God sanctifies us by his grace: but God sanctifies us by his grace that afterward we may be able to work well.
pass_b_english: Eph 2: good works are fruit of new creation—hence not salvation's cause.
Same logic: works follow sanctification (Augustine's order for justification)—sanctified by grace/faith, not works.

choices.why: God prepares us for works, not works as prior cause.
